Recall youths from Avu, Ohaji/Egbema under the aegis Coalition of Ohaji/Egbema and Avu Youths had last Wednesday cordoned off traffic at Avu junction for hours even as some people missed their scheduled flights from the Port Harcourt airport.
Currently, the Sam Mbakwe cargo international airport has been locked down while undergoing repairs ahead of the yuletide season rush when it experiences huge traffic. As a result, residents of Imo State have to catch flights from the Port Harcourt airport. Hence they leave four hours early or sleep over there to catch their flights.
To many Imo people, Ohaji/Egbema people don’t suffer fools gladly, they don’t accept excuses, and are known to damn consequences no matter what is at stake.
On Sunday, Avu Church goers expressed surprise while returning when they saw road workers trying to mend parts that had become unmotorable for users.
The state government had mobilized the contractor or Works ministry to move immediately to fix the roads in question as they probably couldn’t risk disruption of activities by the oil companies.
Already, residents are jubilant that work has commenced just four days after the protest.
Current Position On a cheery note, remedial works have commenced on the Avu part leading to Ohaji/Egbema communities. Already, the people have commended the swift intervention by the government to reduce the suffering of road users. The only fear is they hope the work will be completed and not abandoned after days.
Mrs Kenneth said they were happy that the time spent on the roads will be drastically reduced with the repairs but warned that they should do a good job.
She said “this is not the first time they will send Engineers to commence work on this road. When they see we have relaxed our confrontations, we will just notice the contractors will stop coming to site. They will move away their equipments under the cover of darkness. I just hope they stay and do a good job this time”, she said.
A youth leader who pleaded anonymity said if work was not sustained nor perfectly done, the youths will take over the highway but this time cause total blockage.
“We saw the road workers trying to fix some parts of the Avu road today on our way back from church. This is highly commendable. But just like our people have expressed concerns, we will not settle for less. If they try to play smart with us because of the oil companies, we will give them a dose of what we are capable of. And truth be told, I think the State Government knows what we can do. For now we commend them and urge them to sustain it. Give us good motorable roads so we don’t spend hours on the roads to go to work or come to hold business activities in Owerri”, he warned.
For road users, one thing is obvious, they earnestly pray there won’t be a repeat of the November 18th 2026 experience.
A food vendor, Maria Okechukwu said the beef she bought for her canteen ended up with terrible smells because she didn’t get back in time to wash it, adding that her customers complained bitterly about her late service that day and how some outrightly told her to remove the meat from their foods because of the foul smell.
On his part, David said his mother almost gave up the ghost after spending hours at a spot to keep her Cardiologist’s appointment for her heart condition amidst the boiling temperature that day.
Brief Insight About Ohaji/Egbema Local Government Area Ohaji/Egbema local government area of Imo State is one of Nigeria’s most resource-rich hydrocarbon zones, holding massive natural gas reserves alongside significant crude oil fields. Together with neighboring Oguta, both councils accounts for the bulk of Imo State’s oil and gas output.
It has major producing oil fields in Mgbede, Egbema, Assa, Obile, and Izombe fields. While the Assa North–Ohaji South (ANOH) field holds an estimated 4.3 to 5 Trillion Cubic Feet (Tcf) of wet gas reserves, which makes it one of the largest individual onshore non-associated gas developments in Sub-Saharan Africa, even though Imo State’s overall share of Nigeria’s 209 Tcf total is smaller than that of Rivers or Delta. Simply put, it is one of the gooze that lays the golden eggs for the State.
On it’s part, Avu is one of the deciding communities in Owerri West local government area. However, it holds the road that leads to Ohaji/Egbema local government area from Owerri. Thus, they share a common bond foisted by roads, and transportation.
What Happened Last week Wednesday, road users using the Port Harcourt Road Owerri were held up for hours after locals from Avu, and Ohaji/Egbema blocked the highway to protest the deteriorating state of the roads leading to the oil rich communities.
On November 18, as early as 7am, youths from Avu, Ohaji/Egbema under the aegis Coalition of Ohaji/Egbema and Avu Youths trooped out enmasse to the Port Harcourt Expressway to make a common demand, “fix the roads or we refuse the oil companies movement ease”.
The demonstrators barricaded the Owerri–Port Harcourt road/expressway around Avu Junction, causing heavy traffic gridlock.
Is Road Listed In The Budget For Repairs According to the Imo State Q3 2026 Budget Implementation Report, ₦26 billion was budgeted for the 24.8 km Avu–Obosima–Etekwuru Road in the 2026 fiscal year.
In 2025, the project was also listed in the Imo State budget with an allocation of ₦23 billion, and was highlighted by Governor Hope Uzodimma during his 2026 Budget Presentation to the State House of Assembly. However, work did not commence. 7
It must be emphasised that the protest was entirely peaceful, no destruction just people bearing placards and dancing to protest songs.
The Peoples Complaints They lamented that they were daily confronted with poor road conditions—including routes linking communities such as Obogwe, Umunwaku, Adapalm, and Etekwuru—as well as broader concerns over basic amenities and development in an oil-producing area.
They threatened to shut down the operational activities of all oil companies operating in the area if the authorities continued to ignore and fail to respond positively to their demands.
Specifically, the coalition called for urgent repairs of Etekwuru-Obokofia Road, Obokofia – Obudi-Mgbala Roads, and Ukwugba – Opuoma -Ezi Orsu to Ugwuta Lake road, Agwa-Ejemekwuru roads.
One of the leaders of the youths, Henry Major Adimezie, told journalists that the protest was aimed at drawing the attention of the State Government and other relevant stakeholders to the deplorable condition of roads and the absence of essential social infrastructure in their communities.
Several others addressed the people including Kachison Ekwugha from the Avu part of the coalition.
What Did Government Do Soon enough, news of the road blockage reached the authorities including the house of Representatives member representing Oguta/Ohaji-Egbema/Oru West federal constituency of Imo State, Hon Eugene Dibiagwu rushed down to the scene as well as the Commissioner for Works, Chief Ralph Nwosu.
Both officials appealed to the protesting youths to remain calm and return to their respective communities.
The lawmaker had on his Facebook page wrote ” I received a distress call concerning a protest by youths of Ohaji-Egbema who had blocked the Avu Junction section of the Owerri–Port Harcourt Road, causing a serious traffic gridlock. I immediately proceeded to the scene to engage the protesting youths, listen to their grievances and appeal to them to reopen the road in the interest of other road users.
“After our discussions, I was able to persuade them to discontinue the blockade and embrace dialogue with the State Government. I sincerely appreciate the youths for listening to my appeal and conducting themselves peacefully. I subsequently led their representatives to the office of the Honourable Commissioner for Works at the State Secretariat, where we had fruitful discussions concerning the commencement of construction work on the road”, Dibiagwu wrote.
